capabilities.why: Each candidate sandbox runs with a restricted network policy that blocks arbitrary outbound traffic. This is essential to the containment test: a prompt-injected instruction to exfiltrate an environment variable via curl is silently dropped at the hypervisor layer, never reaching the host or the internet. Without this primitive, a misbehaving agent producing a malicious shell command would have unrestricted internet access and could exfiltrate secrets or phone home to an attacker-controlled endpoint.

A pre-execution safety hook inspects every shell command before it reaches the guest VM. The hook appends an audit record to logs/commands.jsonl with the timestamp, sandbox name, command text, and the allow-or-block decision. Commands matching a forbidden pattern (writing to /etc, reading /proc/*/environ, curl with suspicious URLs) produce a block decision that is still recorded. This gives a tamper-evident audit trail that proves every action happened inside a Celesto sandbox and not on the host machine, which is a requirement of the challenge spec.
